1) 'git pull --rebase' -> 'git pull --rebase=merges'. Plain --rebase flattens merge commits, so a task/* branch that had updated itself by merging main got the merged side replayed commit by commit and hit a modify/delete conflict every time. Reproduced in a throwaway repo before writing the fix, and both variants compared.
2) The result is now CHECKED. 2>/dev/null threw the conflict away, || true ate the exit code, git push ran against a repository sitting mid-rebase, and the script printed 'done.'. 3) Found while writing the tests: no answer meant YES. read ... || a='' fell through to the [y] default, so a run with neither a terminal nor readable stdin (CI, headless Ralph, a hook) pushed unasked, in a script whose first line promises it never pushes silently. Now: no readable answer = no.
